agent-input.title: Untrusted content enters an agent session
agent-input.hypothesis: An agent ingests external content or an untrusted session identifier before a tool action or configuration change outside the approved task.
telemetry: Input provenance, source type and request/session identifier
Captured tool responses or retrieved content where collection is approved
Subsequent tool calls, configuration changes and approval decisions
investigate: Join the ingested input to later actions by session or request ID; preserve the original content as evidence.
Compare the resulting action with the approved task and baseline. Receiving suspicious text alone is not successful injection.
agent-input.limitation: Requires application instrumentation and a custom field mapping. Input exposure does not prove that the model followed instructions, executed a tool or bypassed approval. Avoid collecting sensitive prompt bodies unless authorized.
agent-input.query_scope: Custom-schema candidate for input exposure only. Map agent.input.ingest and agent.session.resume to your application request and session logs. CorrelationId must link subsequent actions. EventType values are proposed normalization names, not native vendor events.

agent-tools.limitation: Process logs cannot recover model intent. Remote connectors and in-process interpreters may produce no local child process. Prompt content alone is not a reliable signature.

bedrock.title: Bedrock discovery / key testing

linux-webshell.title: Linux web worker → shell / interpreter
linux-webshell.hypothesis: A PHP or web-server worker launches a shell, interpreter, or reconnaissance utility outside its normal baseline.
telemetry: Linux process creation (EDR / auditd normalized to process fields)
File changes to web roots and PHP configuration
investigate: Trace the worker's children and correlate them with inbound requests.
Review auto_prepend_file, .bashrc changes, /dev/shm execution, and outbound tunnels where the report describes them.
linux-webshell.limitation: Legitimate CGI, maintenance, and deployment scripts can match. The query is a process-tree starter, not a complete web-shell detector.
linux-webshell.query_scope: linux process candidates. Sigma needs normalized process events; KQL needs Defender coverage for that OS; SPL uses a custom openattacks:process sourcetype with Sysmon-style Image / ParentImage / CommandLine fields. Map raw auditd or Endpoint Security data first.

queries.sigma:
title: Hunt - Linux web worker → shell / interpreter
id: 068e005a-876e-4ba3-a414-791f9a1c2330
status: experimental
description: A PHP or web-server worker launches a shell, interpreter, or
  reconnaissance utility outside its normal baseline.
author: MagicSword OpenAttacks catalog
date: 2026-10-23
references:
  - https://github.com/MHaggis/Security-Detections-MCP
falsepositives:
  - Authorized activity matching this broad hunt; baseline and investigate
    before alerting.
level: low
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - /sh
      - /bash
      - /python
      - /python3
      - /curl
      - /wget
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - /php-fpm
      - /php-fpm8.2
      - /apache2
      - /httpd
      - /nginx
  condition: selection
queries.kql:
// Draft hunt; requires Defender for Endpoint process telemetry for this OS.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("sh", "bash", "python", "python3", "curl", "wget")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm", "php-fpm8.2", "apache2", "httpd", "nginx")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA1
| order by Timestamp desc
queries.spl:
sourcetype="openattacks:process"
Image IN ("*/sh", "*/bash", "*/python", "*/python3", "*/curl", "*/wget")
ParentImage IN ("*/php-fpm", "*/php-fpm8.2", "*/apache2", "*/httpd", "*/nginx")
| table _time host User Image CommandLine ParentImage ParentCommandLine
| sort - _time

metadata.hypothesis: An agent tool reaches a metadata endpoint and the resulting role identity is used outside its intended task or resource scope.
investigate: Look for metadata destination access from the agent's execution context and determine which credentials were available.
Trace that role session into agent memory, secrets and other resources; review the permissions boundary.
metadata.limitation: Metadata traffic may stay on the host and be absent from ordinary proxy logs. IMDS access can be legitimate; correlate the role and task.

windows-install.title: Unapproved Windows program execution
windows-install.hypothesis: A newly downloaded or staged executable runs from a user-writable location and exhibits the reported follow-on behavior.
telemetry: File certificate information and application-control audit / block events
investigate: Verify publisher, hash, origin, prevalence and local approval rather than trusting a product name or signature.
Trace child processes and related credential, network or persistence events.
windows-install.limitation: Many approved installers run from user-writable folders. These events are hunt candidates, not proof of malware or an enforced block.
windows-install.query_scope: Windows process candidates. Sigma uses normalized process_creation fields; KQL requires Defender for Endpoint; SPL requires the Sysmon XML sourcetype. Tune collectors, fields and baselines before use.

windows-shell.title: Suspicious Windows script execution
windows-shell.hypothesis: A script host or shell runs encoded content, a remote URL, or inline script syntax, then downloads or launches a payload.
telemetry: Windows process creation: Sysmon Event 1 or Defender DeviceProcessEvents
investigate: Follow the parent and child process tree and recover the script or URL from logs without executing it.
Correlate the payload's signer/hash, persistence, and network activity; baseline approved automation.
windows-shell.limitation: Encoded commands and remote administration can be legitimate. This does not cover every script host, in-process execution, or non-Windows branch.
windows-shell.query_scope: Windows process candidates. Sigma uses normalized process_creation fields; KQL requires Defender for Endpoint; SPL requires the Sysmon XML sourcetype. Tune collectors, fields and baselines before use.

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "mshta.exe", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "-enc" or ProcessCommandLine contains "http" or ProcessCommandLine contains "FromBase64String" or ProcessCommandLine contains "javascript:" or ProcessCommandLine contains "vbscript:"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA1
| order by Timestamp desc
queries.spl:
sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1
Image IN ("*\\powershell.exe", "*\\pwsh.exe", "*\\mshta.exe", "*\\wscript.exe", "*\\cscript.exe")
CommandLine IN ("*-enc*", "*http*", "*FromBase64String*", "*javascript:*", "*vbscript:*")
| table _time host User Image CommandLine ParentImage ParentCommandLine
| sort - _time
